newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo attacks opposition publicity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo attacks opposition publicity.

text.p: Mexico's President Ernesto Zedillo has lashed out at the opposition parties running in the mid-term elections in July, attacking their publicity as an attempt to fool the public.

"We have to draw your attention to those who do not do much because they hate capitalism, but who are now using the techniques of capitalism to try to fool the people," Zedillo said in a speech Friday in the southern city of Villahermosa.

"They are using publicity like people trying to sell potato chips, beer and soda pop to tell people that like this they can resolve their problems," Zedillo said, according to a report in the Reforma newspaper Saturday.

Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) is locked in a tough battle with opposition conservative National Action Party (PAN) and the left-wing Party of the Democractic Revolution (PRD) before the July 6 elections.
All three parties, and some smaller ones, have flooded television and radio with hard-hitting advertisements.
Mexicans will vote for a new lower house in Congress, as well as part of the Senate, governors in six states and the mayor of Mexico City.
